According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, and pointed out that the integration "performed far below expectations" after its launch in 2024. The details are as follows.

OpenAI requests the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk stated that X, now merged into SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over alleged collusion to exclude AI competitors. The incident stemmed from OpenAI's agreement with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the lawsuit was formally filed, the actual scope of the allegations went beyond the App Store ranking issues that Musk initially publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of attempting to stifle the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to transform itself into an "everything app."

In the following weeks and months, the involved companies successively submitted arguments, allegations, and defences to the court. Apple and OpenAI argued that the agreement was not an exclusive partnership as alleged; at the same time, the court documents also revealed new details about the inside of the collaboration between the two parties.

One of these details was exposed in a document submitted by OpenAI today. As first reported by the Financial Times, OpenAI "said it was disappointed with the tepid response from Apple users to ChatGPT." The two parties reached an agreement in 2024 for ChatGPT to power "Apple Intelligence."

The report is as follows:

Court documents submitted on Wednesday indicated that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI expected to benefit from Apple's promotional and brand association effects, gaining a "halo effect," and attracting more Apple Intelligence users to subscribe. However, one month after the launch of the ChatGPT integration, "the start appeared slow," and OpenAI therefore lowered its forecast for weekly active users. The documents continued to state that by the summer of 2025, "Apple's integration of ChatGPT had clearly performed below expectations."

The report pointed out that the documents submitted today contained multiple redacted sections of dialogue, but the unredacted portions showed that OpenAI executives were concerned that Apple might "want to accelerate the pace" and seek another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately hoped to allow users to choose different AI models, and explicitly mentioned Gemini as a potential future collaboration option.

That particular collaboration ultimately failed to materialise, but Apple subsequently switched to using Google's Gemini model to power the all-new Siri AI; Xcode has also been expanded to support coding agents from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Returning to today's documents, the Financial Times noted that the documents also mentioned that the way Apple rolled out ChatGPT might be one of the reasons for the low adoption rate, given that the integration feature is turned off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recently submitted securities disclosure documents undermine SpaceXAI's claim that the Apple partnership harms competition. OpenAI stated in the documents that SpaceX's IPO registration statement "is filled with disclosures that are completely contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

Based on the above reasons, OpenAI is requesting Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled for trial next January.
